dossier.architecture: First-year swerve scorer with carefully staged cargo and a reverted climber.

subsystems.drivetrain: First swerve season after differential drive; team emphasized driver practice.
subsystems.intake: Nonparallel four-bar with carbon/foam roller and printed mecanum features; passive deployed flap bridges the bumper gap.
subsystems.transfer: Single-roller ramp; wrong-color cargo rejected using an alternative turret aim.
subsystems.scoring: Aluminum/nitrile main wheel with brass inertia disks; back wheels reduce spin. Wheel idles throughout the match and changes speed with range.
subsystems.endgame: First-regional pivot/telescope replaced by faster four-stage design at regional 2; reliability problems led to a return to original architecture for Worlds with wider hooks and a second rear hook. Reported 15–20 seconds.
subsystems.controls: LED shooter-readiness feedback supports driver decisions.

versions: Three distinct climber states: original, faster replacement, revised original at Worlds.
dossier.analysis: A reverted design is a real season evolution, not missing progress. Count successful retained climbs and total match contribution rather than treating a faster prototype as a superior final robot.

context_documents.body:
# 2022-5172: A fast rejected climb is not the same as a useful fielded climb

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A nonparallel four-bar and passive bumper-gap flap feed a ramp and turreted launcher with added brass inertia. The team says a faster two-arm climb had mechanical problems, so it reverted and widened hooks to clear the turret/reduce swing.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The source explicitly prioritizes the revised reliable climb over the failed fast alternative.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Useful timing includes completion probability and physical interference. A turret that scores well can still block the climb’s swept envelope. Continuous wheel idling also has an electrical/thermal cost that should be measured.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test hook clearance over turret range, climb swing and repeated-volley wheel recovery.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
